Recent notes (11/18/2026 by Jenn Jeanquart, 11/11/2026 by Jenn Jeanquart, 11/06/2026 by Jenn Jeanquart): Client Status & Recent Progress

Program Timeline: Currently in Week 3 of the program, with a scheduled release date of January 14.
Employment & Halfway House: Client secured a current work assignment/job, allowing him more freedom to leave the halfway house.
Restrictions: Curren

**Latest Case Note Updates:** [Update 11/18/2026 • Jenn Jeanquart]: Client Status & Recent Progress

Program Timeline: Currently in Week 3 of the program, with a scheduled release date of January 14.
Employment & Halfway House: Client secured a current work assignment/job, allowing him more freedom to leave the halfway house.
Restrictions: Currently on a phone restriction stemming from the previous week (originally two weeks, reduced to one week due to good behavior and lack of prior infractions in BOP). He receives his phone back when leaving for work and gets off restriction tomorrow.
Social & Family Support: Client reports positive engagement, spending time with his girlfriend and speaking more frequently with his children.
Barriers & Re-entry Planning (Pre-Job Placement "Gates")

Home Confinement: Client noted difficulty getting his address approved for home confinement, though he is unbothered by it given his upcoming January 14 release date.
Driver’s License: Client has not yet visited the DMV to address license reinstatement (previously noted ~$200+ in fees and potential tickets to clear) because work hours conflict with DMV closing times (5:00 PM).
Plan: Client will request a pass from his case manager (Ms. Phillips or Ms. McMullen) to take an Uber directly from work to the DMV on Monday, Tuesday, or Wednesday of next week (as the DMV is closed the Friday after Thanksgiving).
Vocational Training (SkillCat & Forklift):
Client has completed 3 total SkillCat modules (2 within the last five working days), including welding and electrician modules. Advised to aim for 3 modules per week.
Forklift training is pending; caseworker plans to schedule him within the next couple of weeks.
Employment Goals: Open to various industries (preferring to avoid fast food) with a desire for decent pay and opportunities to learn a new skill/trade prior to returning home in January.
Medical & Mental Health

Physical Health: Client experiences intermittent heart arrhythmia/fluttering. He reports his doctor confirmed it is not serious and it does not prevent him from working. He also has asthma and keeps an inhaler on him.
Mental Health: Prescribed anxiety medication through BOP and attends counseling at Innovative Solutions. Client expressed that he does not feel the counseling is particularly helpful yet, noting he copes best with anxiety by calling his mother or talking to someone to distract himself.
Action Items / Next Steps

Client: Submit a pass request to Ms. Phillips or Ms. McMullen to visit the DMV next week (Mon–Wed) to address license reinstatement and check for outstanding tickets.
Client: Continue working toward the goal of completing 3 SkillCat modules per week.
Caseworker: Coordinate forklift training for the client and his peer (Justin) within the next two weeks.
Caseworker: Follow up on job placement readiness after Week 4 requirements ("gates") are cleared. | [Update 11/11/2026 • Jenn Jeanquart]: 1. Employment & Job Search
Inquiry Regarding "James Emmett & Co.": Client inquired about an unexpected text message/screening regarding a warehouse/machine operator role in Lexington paying $16/hour, purportedly connected to Novo Staffing via Indeed. Worker and client reviewed the lead together and identified several red flags, including a lack of verifiable physical address and an out-of-state area code (920). The client opted not to pursue the lead due to safety and legitimacy concerns.
Transportation Feasibility: Discussed transit options to Lexington if future employment is secured there; noted bus lines run near Lexington Medical Center, though last-mile walking or rides from friends would be required.
Program Alignment & Expectations: Reminded client he is currently in Week 2 of the program. Reviewed program benchmarks: formal job applications and employer introductions typically begin around Week 4 to target sustainable positions offering at least $17–$20+/hour rather than rushing into lower-paying opportunities. Client acknowledged the importance of patience and leveraging the program’s direct employer relationships and vouching system.
Resume & Work History Update: Reviewed client’s draft resume for upcoming revisions. Captured previous employment details from 2019: forklift/material handling experience at DHL Supply Chain (Adidas/Reebok warehouse).
Upcoming Job Fairs: Discussed attendance at tomorrow's hiring event featuring Scout Motors (manufacturing/assembly) and reviewed second-chance hiring considerations regarding criminal background checks.
2. Driver’s License Reinstatement
Status: Client reported his driver’s license is suspended due to an outstanding fee/ticket. Worker previously identified a reinstatement fee of ~$200+, though client does not recall the original citation.
Plan: Because electronic records accessible by staff do not list specific jurisdiction details, client must visit the DMV in person to obtain citation numbers and originating court information (e.g., Richland County or City of Columbia).
Facility Pass: Client explained halfway house pass procedures (passes must be requested prior to Tuesday). Client will request a pass next week to visit the DMV after program hours.
3. Halfway House & Supervision Environment
Adjustment & Frustrations: Client expressed ongoing tension with residential facility staff, noting interactions often feel punitive or similar to prison.
De-escalation Application: Client reflected on a recent incident where he felt provoked by a facility staff member (Mr. Turner). Rather than reacting impulsively, client stepped back, retrieved his visitation slip, processed the situation, and delivered a sincere apology. Worker affirmed client's successful use of cognitive-behavioral skills learned in group to manage emotional responses and avoid disciplinary infractions.
Case Manager / BOP Status: Client discussed recent friction with his facility case manager (Ms. McMullen) regarding facility pass coordination and his medical follow-up appointments. He noted she raised the possibility of returning him to a BOP medical yard due to hospital visits, which caused significant stress. Client remains determined to manage his health appointments properly while staying in the community.
4. Health & Wellness
Cardiac Concerns: Client reported managing irregular heartbeat/arrhythmia episodes that began around February/March. He has followed up with cardiology and received hospital testing; no daily prescription was mandated other than following up on anxiety/stress management.
Coping Strategies: Client acknowledged anxiety heavily triggers his physical symptoms. Identified effective coping mechanisms, including calling support contacts, resting, taking deep breaths, and vocalizing emotions rather than suppressing them.
5. Action Plan & Next Steps
Client: Submit a pass request at the residential facility next week to attend the DMV after program hours to retrieve specific court/ticket details for license reinstatement.
Client: Attend the scheduled job fair tomorrow and engage with employers (Scout Motors).
Worker: Finalize formatting and update dates/work experience for client’s resume and print physical copies prior to the job fair.
Worker & Client: Continue daily attendance and cognitive-behavioral curriculum through Week 4 prior to initiating outside job applications. | [Update 11/06/2026 • Jenn Jeanquart]: Program Engagement & General Status:
Client reported that the program is going well, noting that learning new positive skills has been the primary benefit.
Identification & Driver’s License Status:
Reviewed client needs via intake tracking. Client stated he had a learner's permit in the past and holds a regular state ID.
Worker accessed state records using client's identifying information. System records reflect $250.00 in outstanding reinstatement fees across three issues: failure to maintain proof of financial responsibility (SR-22), unpaid traffic ticket, and unpaid property tax.
Worker advised client to visit the DMV next Friday to obtain a full printout of outstanding citations and reinstatement requirements. Noted that program financial assistance may be available to help cover reinstatement fees once specifics are verified.
Client does not have his official birth certificate on hand; reported it was obtained in New Jersey but left with his mother and is currently misplaced.
Family, Health & Daily Living:
Client reports having 5 children (ages 4, 4, 5, 6, and 7) living in Rock Hill, Chester, and Lancaster. No child support orders reported.
Client receives current medical/prescription management through the Bureau of Prisons (BOP).
Reentry Planning & Post-Release Housing:
Current projected release date from the halfway house is January 14th (with potential adjustment based on earned credits).
Housing plans remain unresolved. Client expressed feeling pressure regarding where to parole, noting options include family in Rock Hill or his girlfriend in Gastonia, NC.
Discussed interstate supervision parameters; client was advised to speak with his BOP case manager regarding travel/transfer restrictions for North Carolina (interstate compact), as well as home confinement options.
Discussed how post-release residence directly drives employment placement strategies (e.g., job search in the Columbia area vs. Rock Hill) to avoid premature job disruption.
Employment & Banking Goals:
Client created an Indeed profile and resume independently after file upload issues with a previous draft.
Client’s 90-day short-term goals include successfully discharging from the halfway house, obtaining stable employment, and spending time with his children.
Discussed banking setup: Client will receive his program pay card on Monday; worker recommended using the upcoming Friday errand pass to cash out earnings and open a traditional checking/savings account (reminded client to bring ID, SSN card, and proof of address/mail).
Cognitive Behavioral / Needs Assessment Follow-Up:
Reviewed results from the client's computerized assessment to address past behavioral patterns:
Work & Skills Training: Addressed past patterns of leaving jobs when frustrated or having workplace peer conflicts.
Accountability & Interpersonal Regulation: Discussed triggers related to feeling disrespected, conflict de-escalation, receiving supervisor feedback, and accepting accountability.
Action Steps / Next Steps
Client:
Submit pass request to visit the DMV next Friday to obtain official license status/fee breakdown printout.
Coordinate with BOP case manager regarding post-release residence requirements and interstate supervision rules for NC vs. SC.
Bring state ID, SSN, and mail to a local branch next Friday to establish a personal bank account.
Continue exploring permanent housing options and report final release address to worker.
Case Manager / Program:
Pick up client’s program pay card in Charleston and deliver by Monday.
Review client’s updated Indeed profile and assist with ongoing resume tailoring.
Coordinate potential fee assistance for driver's license reinstatement once official DMV documentation is submitted.
Align employment placement search with confirmed geographic release plan.
